subject.title: Feature: Built-in pace-aware rate limiting for autonomous agents

question: Should OpenClaw own pace-aware provider usage controls in core, and should the first phase be observability-only or opt-in enforcement?
rationale: The remaining work would add provider-specific semantics, persisted usage state, new agent config, and autonomous scheduling behavior, which source inspection cannot safely choose without maintainer intent.

options.title: Observability First
options.body: Expose pace context in status/session_status and the provider usage contract without blocking work until the data model and provider semantics prove reliable.

options.title: Opt-In Enforcement
options.body: Add disabled-by-default subagent or non-interactive throttling with explicit config, persistence, tests, and operator recovery guidance.

options.title: Plugin/API First
options.body: Keep core lean by designing provider and agent hooks so a plugin can own pace policy without hardcoding Anthropic behavior in core.

recommendation.title: Observability First
recommendation.body: Expose pace context in status/session_status and the provider usage contract without blocking work until the data model and provider semantics prove reliable.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the clearest history on provider usage tracking and adjacent auth/failover configuration, while the decision is product/API direction rather than a current-line repair.
